description:
FILED s543i (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22), found by member 2's probe table (scratch/s543i/probes/m2e.txt row w21 in the s543i worktree): pre-existing, the same on main / the base a8889369 and on the s543i tree.

A NEGATED BAREWORD (perl's string "-foo", toke.c force_word after a unary minus) followed by a binary `-` or `+` is read by PCL as a CALL of a sub named "-foo" with the rest as its argument list:

    no strict; my $x = -foo - 1; print "$x\n";      # perl -1      PCL: Undefined subroutine &main::-foo called
    use strict; my $x = -foo + 1; print "$x\n";     # perl 1       PCL: the same die
    my @a = (-foo, -bar - 1); print "@a\n";         # perl -foo -1 PCL: Undefined subroutine &main::-bar
    no strict; my $x = - foo -1; print "$x\n";      # perl -1      PCL: Undefined subroutine &main::foo

Controls = perl: `-foo` alone, `-foo . "x"`, `-foo x 2`, `-foo * 2`, `-foo < 1`, `(-foo, 1)`, `-foo eq "-foo"`, and a DECLARED `sub foo` (`-foo -1` is -(foo(-1)), probe w22).  PPI gives Word<-foo> Operator<-> Number<1> (and Word<-foo> Number<-1>, which PExpr's _fix_ppi_negative_number_bug splits since s543i because a negated word is a term): the tokens are right; the call reading is PCL's -- a Word followed by an operator that can be unary (`-`, `+`) is taken as a list operator with an operand, which perl never does for a word forced after a unary minus unless it is a declared sub.  Where to look: PExpr's bareword-call decision (the same question _is_zero_arg_func / _word_is_declared_term answer) for a Word whose content starts with `-` (and for `foo` right after a split unary `-`).
Rare in real code (the `-option => value` idiom is autoquoted and unaffected).
subject: LOUD (rare): a negated bareword before a binary minus / plus is called as a sub -- `-foo - 1` dies "Undefined subroutine &main::-foo" (perl: the string "-foo" minus 1 = -1); PPI's tokens are right, the call reading is PExpr's
triage_reason: a run-time die where perl runs, on core syntax (a negated bareword string before a binary - / +); rare
